newsitem.title: USA: The Registry to buy Renaissance Solutions for $430 mln.
newsitem.headline: The Registry to buy Renaissance Solutions for $430 mln.

text.p: Consulting firm The Registry Inc. said Tuesday it will acquire Renaissance Solutions Inc. in a stock deal valued at about $430 million.
News of the plan sent the stock of Registry tumbling, losing $5.50 to $51 in morning trading on Nasdaq.
Registry attributed the decline to investors who may be waiting to see the outcome of the transaction.
Meanwhile, Renaissance Solutions stock was up $3.25 to $38, also on Nasdaq.
Under terms of the acqisition, which was approved by the boards of both companies, Renaissance shareholders will get 0.80 share of Registry for each of their Renaissance shares.
The Registry said it expects to take a one-time pre-tax charge of $11 million to $13 million in the September quarter relating to the acquisition.
Registry Chief Financial Officer Robert Foley said the deal is expected to add five cents per share to earnings in 1997 and 10 cents to 15 cents per share in 1998.
Foley will become chief financial officer of the new company. Drew Conway, president and chief executive officer of Registry, will become the merged company's president and chief executive officer.
Based in Newton, Mass., Registry provides information technology consulting services. Renaissance, based in Lincoln, Mass., develops technology-based business solutions.
"There are a lot of synergies between the two companies...and a lot of opportunities within those synergies," said Foley.
He said there will "absolutely be no job losses" from the merger.
"We are likely to add jobs as we expand," he said.
The companies said the deal would close within the next 90 days, pending regulatory and shareholder approval.
